messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@tidework.co>

Cc: Samir Gupta <s.gupta@tidework.co>

Subject: TideWork onboarding - access, SSO and API key plan

Hi Jonas / Monica,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We’re ready to move from contract-signing to the initial tenant activation and want to lock down the access pattern and timeline. Quick background: we’ll have a small pilot team (6 users) and a production service that will call Redwood for embeddings and chat. Key asks from our side: 

- Confirm SSO vs API-key approach for initial access (we prefer SAML for user access, API keys for the service account).
- Walk through the API key seeding approach for staging -> prod (risk: accidental prod key exposure).
- Roles mapping: we have Admin, Engineer, Analyst — want RBAC recommendations.
- Mutual action plan and dates so we can align procurement and infra.

Attached is an onboarding-matrix (CSV/XLSX) with people + tentative start dates. Can you propose a short plan (3–4 steps) and who on your side will be the technical contact for key rotation and invite cadence?

Attaching: onboarding-matrix.xlsx (see sheet: pilot-users).

Thanks,
Elena
Product Ops | TideWork Analytics

---
Attachment: onboarding-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@tidework.co>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Mar 2028 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TideWork onboarding - access, SSO and API key plan

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and matrix. Below is a compact 4-step plan we use for pilot tenants; I’ve labeled owners and rough dates so you can drop into procurement / infra calendars.

1) Pre-provision & SSO metadata exchange (Day 0–2) — Action: TideWork to send SAML metadata and SP/IDP contact. Owner: TideWork (Elena / Samir). We’ll spin up tenant in staging.

2) Admin invites + temporary prod admin (Day 2–4) — Action: Redwood will invite up to 2 TideWork admins into the tenant (SAML SSO or email invites if SSO delayed). Owner: Jonas (ops). Purpose: set roles & map users. We recommend keeping a single service account for workloads.

3) Service account key seeding and staged keys (Day 4–7) — Action: Redwood to seed a staging API key (scoped) and provide instructions for rotation. For prod we recommend an automated secret manager entry (we can provide a sample script for AWS Secrets Manager / GCP Secret Manager). Owner: Ben Carter (SRE).

4) Smoke tests + go/no-go (Day 7–10) — Action: run sampling of embeddings + chat flows using the staging key, then swap to prod key after verification. Owner: TideWork engineering + Redwood success.

Decisions / notes:
- SAML-first for user access is ideal; we support both SAML (metadata) and SCIM for group sync later, but SCIM is optional for pilot.
- For RBAC: map TideWork Admin -> Redwood Admin (full), Engineer -> Editor (deploy/call), Analyst -> Viewer (read-only dashboards, no key issuance). I’ll attach our role matrix to the Drive link.
- Security: Ben will own key rotation policy and provide a 7-day temporary admin invite process to avoid too many permanent admins.

Next steps for us:
- Elena: send saml-metadata.xml and the two admin emails to invite.
- Ben: I’ve added an internal task to seed a scoped staging key and generate a rotation sample script.
- Monica: could you add the runbook link for the customer?

I’ll follow up with a short mutual action plan once I have the metadata and admin list.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Principal Customer Engineer | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0147

Subject: Re: TideWork onboarding - access, SSO and API key plan

Adding a couple of operational guards from the implementation side:

- Temporary admin invites: we recommend issuing time-limited admin invites (7 days) for initial setup. After the 7 days, we auto-revoke and ask for confirmation to make them permanent. This prevents lingering elevated access during the pilot.
- Service account rotation: Ben, can you produce a sample rotation schedule (7-day rotation for staging keys, 90-day for prod) and a short script (bash + AWS/GCP snippets)?
- Audit trail: we’ll enable tenant-level audit logging for all API key creations and role changes; that will be available in the Console > Admin > Audit for 30 days by default. If TideWork needs longer retention, procurement can add that as an add-on.

I’ve put a short onboarding checklist in the shared drive (link below). If TideWork confirms SAML today, we can start invites Monday.

Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
